Instill.description: Once per day, a kensai of 8th level or higher can use a full-round action to attempt a Concentration check (DC 10 + the target's HD or character level) while touching a willing ally. On a success, the kensai transfers a portion of his combat ability to that ally, reducing his own base attack bonus and/or any combination of his base save bonuses by up to 1 point per class level and granting the same values to the recipient. After 1 hour, the transferred power automatically returns to the kensai. If the ally dies before the power returns, the kensai must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC 5 + the target's HD or character level) or die as well. On a successful save, the kensai immediately recovers all transferred bonuses.

Ki Projection.description: From 4th level onward, a kensai applies half his class level (rounded down) as a bonus to Bluff, Diplomacy, Gather Information, and Intimidate checks. At 8th level, this bonus increases to his full class level. However, if a creature discovers it was deceived by one of the kensai's Bluff checks, that creature receives a +10 bonus on any future check or saving throw against the kensai's Bluff, Diplomacy, Gather Information, or Intimidate attempts. The kensai can restore the creature's trust by improving its attitude from unfriendly to friendly.

Ki Warlord.description: Upon reaching 10th level, a kensai earns widespread renown as a ki warlord. Fellow kensai who share his alignment hold the ki warlord in high esteem, and even those of different alignments show a degree of deference. A ki warlord who serves an NPC master typically receives greater authority and responsibility within that master's domain, potentially being granted control of a castle, monastery, or martial academy. One who serves a deity may find that deity taking a more direct interest, communicating wishes personally or through agents. Beyond these narrative benefits, a ki warlord gains practical advantages. He may call upon lower-level members of the prestige class for aid in his quests or in fulfilling his oath of service, provided such requests do not conflict with those members' own oaths or alignment. Lower-level kensai are expected to provide reasonable assistance, including food, shelter, and access to minor resources that other characters might need to negotiate for. Furthermore, a ki warlord radiates an inspiring presence in battle: allies fighting within 30 feet of him gain a +1 morale bonus on Will saves, Concentration checks, and attack rolls. Lawful allies receive a +2 morale bonus on these same checks instead.

Power Surge.description: Starting at 2nd level, a kensai can spend a move action to attempt a DC 15 Concentration check, focusing his inner energy. On a success, he receives a +8 bonus to Strength lasting a number of rounds equal to half his class level. If he activates this ability more than once within the same 24-hour period, the DC rises by 5 for each subsequent use after the first.

Signature Weapon.description: A kensai selects one weapon he wields (which must be a weapon for which he possesses the Weapon Focus feat) as his signature weapon. Swords and bows are common choices, though even natural weapons are valid selections. Manufactured weapons must be at least masterwork quality. When entering this prestige class, the kensai develops a supernatural bond with his chosen signature weapon, channeling a portion of his life force into it. This bond enhances the weapon's effectiveness, but only when wielded by the kensai himself.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This prestige class does not grant proficiency with any weapons or armor.

Withstand.description: At 5th level and beyond, whenever a kensai must attempt a Reflex save against an area-effect spell (such as fireball), he may substitute a Concentration check in place of the Reflex save to avoid taking full damage. If the kensai possesses evasion or improved evasion, those abilities function normally with this Concentration check.

The character focuses part of his life energy on the weapon, making it more effective in his hands and his hands alone.

classFeatures.name: Power Surge

classFeatures.description: Once per day, a kensai of 8th level or higher may take a full-round action to make a Concentration check (DC 10 + target's HD or character level) to impart some of his own ability into a willing ally he can touch. The kensai then transfers some of his power to the ally: He subtracts up to 1 point per class level from his base attack bonus and/or any or all of his base save bonuses and transfers the same amount to the recipient. The kensai regains the instilled power 1 hour later, when it transfers back out of the ally. If the ally dies before the instilled power is transferred back, the kensai must make a Fortitude save (DC 5 + target's HD or character level) or die as well. If he succeeds, he immediately gets his instilled powers back.
classFeatures.name: Instill

classFeatures.description: When a kensai attains 10th level, he gains great notoriety and becomes known as a ki warlord. Other kensai of the same alignment revere the ki warlord, and even those of differing alignments treat him with some measure of respect. If the ki warlord has an NPC master, this master likely assigns the ki warlord more responsibility and authority within his domain (perhaps giving him a castle, monastery, or military school). If the ki warlord serves a deity, that deity may take a personal interest in giving the ki warlord more responsibility, perhaps actually contacting the ki warlord directly or through intermediaries and making the deity's wishes known. In addition to this added responsibility, a ki warlord gains some tangible benefits. He has the right to petition other (lower-level) members of the prestige class for assistance on adventures or in the fulfillment of his oath. As long as a ki warlord's requests do not violate the other members' own oaths of service or alignment, lower-level kensai have a responsibility to assist a ki warlord in any reasonable manner - such as providing food and shelter, access to minor resources, and other things another character might have to barter for. Ki warlords inspire those around them. When fighting within 30 feet of a ki warlord, allies gain a +1 morale bonus on Will saves, Concentration checks, and attack rolls. Lawful allies gain a +2 morale bonus on these checks.
